features.title: Firebase project setup
features.user_visible_behavior: App connects to Firebase; Firestore, Auth, Storage, and Cloud Functions are all reachable from the mobile app
verification: Run `firebase projects:list` and confirm the project appears
Run `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules,firestore:indexes` with no errors
Open mobile app; confirm Firebase initialises without console errors
features.evidence: ./init.sh passes: all three packages (mobile/, functions/, dashboard/) install and compile with 0 TypeScript errors. firebase.json, firestore.rules, firestore.indexes.json present at repo root. Steps 2 and 3 require a real Firebase project — fill .env files and update .firebaserc before deploying.
features.notes: Scaffold complete. Remaining: connect real Firebase project credentials and run firebase deploy --only firestore:rules,firestore:indexes.

features.title: User registration and login
features.user_visible_behavior: User can sign up with email/password or continue anonymously; `currentUser` is non-null after login; user document created in Firestore `users` collection
verification: Register a new user with email + password; confirm success toast
Check Firebase Auth console — user appears
Check Firestore `users` collection — document created with uid, role='resident', reportCount=0
Log out and log back in; session persists
features.evidence: hooks/useAuth.ts: onAuthStateChanged + ensureUserDoc creates Firestore users doc on first sign-in. app/auth.tsx: email/password login+signup + anonymous. _layout.tsx: useSegments guard redirects unauthenticated users to /auth. TypeScript: 0 errors. Requires EXPO_PUBLIC_* .env filled + Anonymous auth enabled in Firebase console.
features.notes: Anonymous auth requires enabling in Firebase console: Authentication > Sign-in method > Anonymous. Email/Password is sufficient for the demo.

features.title: User home location setup
features.user_visible_behavior: On first login, user is prompted to set home location (auto-filled from GPS, editable on map). `homeGeohash` is written to the Firestore user document. Without this, FCM alerts cannot be targeted.
verification: First login → home location prompt appears
Tap 'Use my location' → GPS coordinate auto-fills
Confirm → Firestore user document has `homeLat`, `homeLng`, `homeGeohash` set
Navigate to Profile and edit home location → Firestore updates
features.evidence: useAuth.ts: onSnapshot listener on users doc; exposes needsHomeSetup=!homeGeohash. _layout.tsx: redirects to /home-setup when needsHomeSetup is true (waits for profile load before redirecting). home-setup.tsx: Location.getCurrentPositionAsync + geohashForLocation precision 7 + updateDoc. profile.tsx: shows coords and Edit button navigating to /home-setup?edit=1. TypeScript: 0 errors. Requires live device test to move to passing.
features.notes: Critical path for push notifications. homeGeohash must be set or users never receive alerts.

features.title: Flood report submission
features.user_visible_behavior: User taps Report button; GPS auto-fills location; user selects depth; tapping Submit writes a document to Firestore `reports` collection; ConfirmToast appears; pin appears on map within ~15 seconds
verification: Tap Report button → ReportSheet slides up
GPS location auto-fills (latitude + longitude shown)
Select each depth option (ankle/knee/waist/chest) — color changes correctly per DEPTH_CONFIG
Tap Submit → ConfirmToast appears
Check Firestore `reports` collection — document created with correct fields: lat, lng, geohash, depth, userId, status='pending', trustScore=60, corroborationCount=1, expiresAt=reportedAt+6h
Confirm `onReportCreate` Cloud Function ran (check Firebase Function logs)
features.evidence: ReportSheet.tsx: addDoc with lat/lng/geohash(precision 7)/depth/reportedAt/expiresAt(+6h)/userId/accountAgeDays(computed from metadata.creationTime)/upvotes=0/downvotes=0/status=pending/corroborationCount=1/trustScore=60. ConfirmToast rendered as sibling to ScrollView inside wrapper View (position:absolute anchored correctly). After 2s navigates to map tab. useLocation.tsx: useFocusEffect re-fetches GPS on each tab focus. TypeScript: 0 errors. Requires live device test + onReportCreate Cloud Function deploy to move to passing.
features.notes: geohash must use precision 7. expiresAt must be exactly reportedAt + 6 hours. onReportCreate Cloud Function needs to be deployed to Firebase to verify trust pipeline.

features.title: Live map with real-time flood pins
features.user_visible_behavior: Map screen shows colored pins for all active (non-expired) reports. Pins update in real time via Firestore listener. Pin color matches DEPTH_CONFIG. Tapping a pin shows depth, time, and upvote/downvote buttons.
verification: Open map screen — no errors in console
Submit a test report from a second device/account → pin appears on map without refresh
Verify pin color: ankle=amber, knee=coral, waist=red, chest=darkred
Expire a report manually (set expiresAt to now) → pin disappears within one listener cycle
Tap a pin → detail sheet shows depth label, time since report
features.notes: useReports hook must filter by status in ['pending','confirmed'] and expiresAt > now().

features.title: Flood-aware route overlay (Option A)
features.user_visible_behavior: User types a destination in the search bar that floats above the map. A blue polyline route is drawn on the map. Each flood report within 200m of the route is ringed with a colored warning circle. A banner shows '3 flood zones on your route · 18 mins (5.2 km)' or 'Route looks clear · 12 mins (3.1 km)'. Tapping × clears the route.
verification: Type a destination and press Search → blue route polyline appears on map
Flood report within 200m of route → colored warning circle appears + banner shows flood count
Flood report > 200m from route → no warning circle, banner shows 'Route looks clear'
Tap × → route and circles clear from map
Missing EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_DIRECTIONS_API_KEY → error banner shown
TypeScript: 0 errors in mobile/
features.notes: Requires EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_DIRECTIONS_API_KEY in mobile/.env (Google Maps Directions API). No new npm packages — polyline decoding is implemented inline in mobile/lib/routeUtils.ts. Flood proximity threshold: 200m from any route segment.

features.title: Corroboration counter and confirmed status
features.user_visible_behavior: When 3 independent reports arrive within 500m and 30 minutes of each other, the earliest report's status changes to 'confirmed' and its pin changes appearance (e.g. solid fill vs outline). `corroborationCount` on each report reflects self-inclusive count.
verification: Submit 3 reports from 3 different user accounts within 500m (use simulated coordinates if needed)
Check Firestore — third report triggers status='confirmed' on the cluster
Verify corroborationCount = nearby.length + 1 on each report doc
Confirm confirmed pin has distinct visual state on map
features.notes: corroborationCount is self-inclusive (own report + nearby). Threshold is >= 3. onReportCreate must query within 500m radius and 30-minute window.

features.title: Severity fast-path preliminary alert
features.user_visible_behavior: A single waist or chest depth report with trustScore >= 65 immediately triggers a push notification to nearby users, labelled 'Unverified report nearby'. This fires without waiting for 3 corroborations.
verification: Submit a 'chest' depth report from a fresh account (trustScore starts at 60; no penalties should apply for an on-road, rainy-day submission → trustScore >= 65)
Second device within 2km receives FCM notification within ~10 seconds
Notification title includes 'Unverified' or 'Preliminary' label
Check Cloud Function logs — notifyNearby called with preliminary=true
features.notes: trustScore = 60 base. If no GPS penalty and no weather penalty, score stays at 60 — below the 65 threshold. Demo setup must ensure at least one check passes (e.g. simulate rainfall > 1mm). Consider lowering threshold to 60 or adjusting base score to 70 if demo conditions are dry.

features.title: FCM push notifications on confirmed reports
features.user_visible_behavior: When a report reaches confirmed status, all users with homeGeohash within 2km receive an FCM push notification. Tapping the notification opens the map centered on the report.
verification: Set homeGeohash on test user within 2km of test report location
Trigger confirmation (3 corroborating reports)
FCM notification arrives on test device within ~5 seconds
Notification payload contains: street, depth, reportedAt, reportId
Tap notification → app opens and map centers on the confirmed report
Test user outside 2km does NOT receive notification
features.notes: Query users by homeGeohash range using geohashQueryBounds. Send to all fcmTokens arrays (multi-token support). Handle stale tokens gracefully (FCM returns UNREGISTERED error — remove that token from the array).

features.title: Report auto-expiry (6 hours)
features.user_visible_behavior: Reports older than 6 hours automatically disappear from the live map. The scheduled Cloud Function runs every 30 minutes and sets status='expired' on overdue reports.
verification: Deploy `expireReports` scheduled function (every 30 minutes)
Manually set a report's expiresAt to 1 minute ago in Firestore
Wait for next scheduled run (or manually trigger via Firebase console)
Confirm report status = 'expired' in Firestore
Confirm pin disappears from live map
features.notes: For demo, manually trigger the function rather than waiting 30 minutes. The live map query must filter expiresAt > Timestamp.now().

features.title: Still flooded / Looks clear upvote and downvote
features.user_visible_behavior: Tapping a map pin shows upvote ('Still flooded') and downvote ('Looks clear') buttons. Tapping increments the corresponding counter on the Firestore document. Counts update in real time.
verification: Tap a pin → detail sheet shows current upvote and downvote counts
Tap 'Still flooded' → Firestore upvotes field increments by 1
Tap 'Looks clear' → Firestore downvotes field increments by 1
Second device sees updated counts without refresh
Firestore security rules only allow upvotes/downvotes to be updated (not other fields)
features.notes: Use FieldValue.increment(1) to avoid race conditions. Firestore security rule must restrict update to only ['upvotes','downvotes'] keys.

features.title: Disputed status trigger
features.user_visible_behavior: When a report accumulates downvotes > upvotes + 5 AND downvotes >= 3, an onUpdate Cloud Function sets its status to 'disputed'. Disputed reports show a different visual state on the map.
verification: Set a report to upvotes=0, downvotes=3 via Firestore console
Confirm onUpdate trigger fires and sets status='disputed'
Set upvotes=10, downvotes=20 → status='disputed' (20 > 10+5 and 20>=3)
Set upvotes=10, downvotes=14 → status stays unchanged (14 is not > 10+5=15)
Map shows disputed pins with distinct visual (e.g. grey or strikethrough)
features.notes: Implement as a Firestore onUpdate trigger inside notifyNearby.ts or a new disputeCheck.ts function. Logic: if (downvotes > upvotes + 5 && downvotes >= 3) set status = 'disputed'.

features.title: Optional photo attachment on report
features.user_visible_behavior: After selecting depth, user can optionally add a photo (camera or gallery). Photo uploads to Firebase Storage. photoUrl is stored on the report document.
verification: Tap photo icon in ReportSheet → camera/gallery picker opens
Select a photo → thumbnail previews in the form
Submit → photo uploaded to Firebase Storage, photoUrl set on Firestore document
Photo visible when tapping the pin detail
features.notes: Nice-to-have for demo polish. Required before claude-vision feature.

features.title: Claude Vision image verification badge
features.user_visible_behavior: Reports with photos show a verification badge: green checkmark (YES), red X (NO), or grey question mark (UNCERTAIN/null). Badge updates asynchronously after Claude Vision responds.
verification: Submit a report with a clear flood photo → photoVerified becomes true within ~10s
Submit a report with a non-flood photo (e.g. clear road) → photoVerified becomes false
Submit a report with an ambiguous photo → photoVerified stays null or becomes false
Badge shown correctly in pin detail sheet for all three states
When answer=NO: trustScore decremented by 40 in Firestore document
features.notes: Depends on photo-upload feature. Uses claude-sonnet-4-6. Fire-and-forget from onReportCreate — do not await in the main pipeline.

features.title: Open-Meteo weather plausibility flag
features.user_visible_behavior: Reports submitted during dry weather (rainfall < 1mm) have their trustScore reduced by 15. The report's weatherRainfallMm field is populated. UI shows a weather flag if rainfall was low.
verification: Submit a report; check Firestore — weatherRainfallMm field populated
Simulate a dry-weather submission (mock Open-Meteo to return 0mm) → trustScore = 60 - 15 = 45
Simulate a rainy submission (mock 5mm) → trustScore stays at 60
UI pin or detail shows weather flag icon when weatherRainfallMm < 1
features.notes: Open-Meteo is free, no API key. Endpoint: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude={lat}&longitude={lng}&hourly=precipitation. Runs in parallel with GPS and lastReport lookups.

features.title: Historical flood zone GeoJSON overlay
features.user_visible_behavior: Map shows a semi-transparent polygon overlay of historically flood-prone zones, loaded from a static GeoJSON file bundled with the app.
verification: GeoJSON file present in mobile/assets/
Map shows overlay polygons on load
Overlay is semi-transparent and does not obscure flood pins
Works offline (static file, no network request)
features.notes: Static file — no backend needed. Use Mapbox or Google Maps GeoJSON layer API.

features.title: City authority web dashboard
features.user_visible_behavior: Authority user opens dashboard web app, sees a heatmap of active reports, a sortable table of all reports, and a ClusterAlert banner when >= 5 confirmed reports appear in a 1km radius.
verification: Dashboard loads at localhost:5173 (Vite dev server)
Heatmap shows active report locations from Firestore
ReportTable is sortable by depth, time, trustScore
Submit 5+ reports in a small area → ClusterAlert banner appears
Only users with role='authority' can see the dashboard (auth check at app level)
features.notes: Separate Vite React app in dashboard/. Reads Firestore directly. Authority auth check required at app load.

features.title: Driver mode one-tap report button
features.user_visible_behavior: Users with role='driver' see a persistent large Report button always visible on the map screen. One tap auto-fills location, skips photo, and submits with large depth buttons optimised for stationary tapping.
verification: Log in as a driver account (role='driver')
Map screen shows persistent Report button (not hidden behind tab)
Tapping → depth picker appears with large tap targets
Submit completes in one tap flow without photo step
Resulting Firestore document identical to resident report
features.notes: Driver mode is the core Grab differentiator for the pitch. Prioritise for demo even if listed at priority 25.
